concepts.gloss_en: The act/practice of telling stories of tzaddikim (verbal infinitive) — an action, not the stories themselves

members.note: representative; infinitive לספר = the act of telling

concepts.gloss_en: Narrations/tellings of stories of tzaddikim (nominal construct ספורי) — characterized as mochin de-gadlut

members.note: construct head ספורי (narrations) differs from the infinitive לספר and from bare מעשיות; kept separate per rule 4

concepts.gloss_en: The stories of tzaddikim themselves (the tales as object) — characterized as bechinat or

members.note: bare noun = the stories themselves, distinct from the act/narration of telling them

notes: All three forms co-occur in lm1:234 and are conceptually linked, but they have distinct heads: לספר (verbal act), ספורי (nominalized narration), and מעשיות (the tales themselves). Rule 4 (action/state about X ≠ X; different construct heads ≠ same concept) plus under-merge preference argues for keeping all three separate. A human may choose to merge the two 'telling' forms (לספר / ספורי) if the graph treats them as one storytelling concept.
